messages:
alex: Customer reports chat stream where the initial ~10 tokens arrive immediately, then ~5-8s silence, then the rest flushes. Only happens over websocket; SSE appears fine. They see it across multiple regions.

maria: Can you paste the request id(s) and a tiny repro they used? Also confirm whether this is hosted or Dedicated.

alex: Hosted. Request ID header from their traces: req_0a1b2c3d. Customer gave a minimal wscat repro they ran locally.

alex: ```bash
wscat -c "wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?api_key=REDACTED" \
  -x '{"type":"start","model":"redwood-chat","input":"hello"}'
```

sam: @alex can you check if any fronting proxy (Cloudflare / Fastly) is in the path? Those often coalesce tiny writes and cause the first-frame delay.

raj: Pulled runtime trace for req_0a1b2c3d: "initial chunk 12 bytes written, then 7.2s gap, then remaining stream chunks". Kernel-level TCP stats show small cwnd and delayed ACKs. My hunch: Nagle/auto-coalescing on client or proxy.

maria: Action item: ask customer to try socket.setNoDelay(true) (Node) or disable Nagle in their ws client. Also ask them to try a raw curl SSE repro to see if it's websocket-only.

alex: Sent these to customer and asked for more details (client lib/version, OS, corporate proxy). Also asked them to run tcpdump/ngrep and attach a debug bundle. Provided this curl SSE quick test:

alex: ```bash
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-chat" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"test"}],"stream":true}'
```

sam: If curl SSE reproduces the gap, that's likely server-side flush/scheduler. If only websocket reproduces it, it's client or proxy buffering. Useful to know whether they are behind an enterprise proxy that rewrites/touches websocket frames.

maria: Customer replied: Node 18, ws 8.10, corporate proxy in front (sits in the middle). They attached tcpdump showing small packet coalescing and long inter-packet gaps. They will try socket.setNoDelay(true) and re-test.

alex: Created internal support ticket and pinned req_0a1b2c3d, added the tcpdump archive to the case. Asked customer to upload the debug bundle (ngrep/tcpdump + client logs).

support-bot: Created case SU-8391 and added label streaming-repro.

raj: For eng-runtime — note the kernel timing info. If customer still sees gaps after disabling Nagle, capture a packet-level trace in a staging pod hitting the same backend to rule out our TCP write coalescing. Quick capture command I gave them: `sudo ngrep -d any -W byline port 443 host api.redwood.ai`.

maria: Also suggested an intermediate repro using websocat/wscat from a machine without the corporate proxy to contrast results. Customer said they can test from a home network later today.

alex: Next steps: wait for debug bundle and home-network repro. If they still see it without the proxy, escalate to eng-runtime with packet capture and logs attached. :thumbsup:
